title: Monodromy Defects of 3D Wilson-Fisher Criticality on the Fuzzy Sphere
abstract: Monodromy (twist) line defects arise as the boundaries of topological symmetry surfaces, which are among the simplest non-trivial conformal defects with direct realizations as magnetic vortex in quantum magnets, as Wilson and t Hooft lines of gauge theories, and as the replica twist operators in quantum information theory. However, their interacting dynamics remains difficult to characterize non-perturbatively. Here we design a way to realize the monodromy boundary conditions in the fuzzy-sphere regularization by threading a symmetry-selective Aharonov-Bohm flux through the two poles of the sphere. We apply this construction to the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ twist of the 3D Ising conformal field theory (CFT), $π$-twist of the 3D O(2) CFT and three inequivalent monodromies of O(3) (centre twist, z-axis $π$-twist and the reflection). For each defect, we extract the low-lying defect spectrum together with bulk-to-defect and defect-defect operator product expansion coefficients, which characterize the operators living on the defect line, their mutual interactions, and how they couple to the surrounding critical bulk. Among the low-lying defect primaries resolved in our spectra, we find no relevant scalar perturbation that preserves all the symmetries of the corresponding defect. The relevant deformations identified in our calculations break at least one preserved symmetry, providing evidence that these monodromy defects are stable against symmetry-preserving relevant perturbations. These results establish a systematic set of non-perturbative conformal data for monodromy defects beyond the Ising twist. Our construction therefore turns the symmetry flux into a tunable knob of the fuzzy-sphere regularization, opening a route to exploring the response of critical matter to distinct defects.
summary: This paper develops a systematic, non-perturbative method using the fuzzy-sphere regularization to study monodromy line defects in 3D critical systems. By threading a specific Aharonov-Bohm flux, the authors calculate the defect spectrum for various CFTs, concluding that these defects are stable against symmetry-preserving relevant perturbations.
main_problem: The primary goal is to characterize the interacting dynamics of monodromy (twist) line defects, which are non-trivial conformal defects in 3D critical systems.
main_result: The study found no relevant scalar perturbation among the low-lying defect primaries that preserves all symmetries, suggesting these monodromy defects are stable against symmetry-preserving relevant perturbations.
method: The authors use the fuzzy-sphere regularization to model the defect boundary conditions by threading a symmetry-selective Aharonov-Bohm flux, allowing for the extraction of the defect spectrum and OPE coefficients.
model_or_system: The analysis is applied to 3D Wilson-Fisher Criticality, specifically examining the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ twist of the 3D Ising CFT, the $\pi$-twist of the 3D O(2) CFT, and three inequivalent monodromies of O(3).
key_observables: Low-lying defect spectrum, bulk-to-defect and defect-defect operator product expansion (OPE) coefficients, and scaling dimensions ($\hat{\Delta}$).
important_parameters: The symmetry flux threading the poles of the fuzzy sphere acts as a tunable knob for the regularization.
main_assumptions: The fuzzy-sphere regularization is assumed to provide an exact realization of the required monodromy boundary conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the defect geometry (e.g., $D_g$ as a boundary of $U_g$) and the intersection of the topological surface with a time slice along a meridian.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical problem of characterizing defect dynamics, then details the fuzzy-sphere construction using Aharonov-Bohm flux, and finally applies this framework to calculate and analyze the defect spectrum and stability for specific CFTs (Ising, O(2), O(3)).
why_interesting: The work provides a systematic, non-perturbative method to study defect stability and interactions in critical systems, which is highly relevant for understanding phase transitions in condensed matter systems.
